purpose: Concrete foundation-level records generated from the religious-foundation blueprint. These are starting records for deep carving; each can later receive texts, schools, institutions, demographic observations, places and relationships.

records.name: Judaism
records.core: covenant, Torah, Jewish peoplehood, ethical and ritual life

records.name: Christianity
records.origin: 1st-century Jesus movement in the Second Temple Jewish environment
records.core: Jesus Christ, crucifixion, resurrection, salvation, worship and Christian community

records.name: Islam
records.origin: 7th-century Arabian religious movement associated with Muhammad and the Qur'anic revelation
records.core: tawhid, prophecy, Qur'an, worship, ethical life and judgment

records.name: Hindu traditions
records.origin: Long-duration family developing from Vedic and later Indian traditions
records.core: dharma, karma, samsara, moksha, devotion, ritual and multiple philosophical paths

records.name: Buddhist traditions
records.origin: 5th–4th-century-BCE Buddhist movement associated with Gautama Buddha
records.core: suffering, its causes, liberation, ethical conduct, meditation and wisdom
sacred_places: major Himalayan and East Asian sites

records.name: Sikhism
records.origin: 15th–16th-century Punjab associated with Guru Nanak and the Sikh Gurus
records.core: one God, remembrance, equality, honest work, sharing and disciplined community

records.name: Jainism
records.origin: Ancient Indian śramaṇa tradition; Mahavira is the 24th Tirthankara of the current cycle in Jain tradition
records.core: ahimsa, karma, liberation, ascetic discipline and non-attachment
countries: East African and other diaspora communities

records.name: Baháʼí Faith
records.origin: 19th-century Persia associated with the Báb and Bahá'u'lláh
records.core: unity of humanity and religions, progressive revelation, spiritual and social transformation
texts: authoritative texts of the Baháʼí Faith
countries: global presence; substantial communities across multiple regions

records.name: Daoist traditions
records.origin: Chinese religious and philosophical traditions developing across ancient and medieval periods
records.core: Dao, harmony, cultivation, ritual, longevity and cosmological order in diverse schools

records.name: Shinto
records.origin: Indigenous Japanese ritual traditions with ancient roots and later institutional development
records.core: kami, purification, shrine ritual, festivals and relationship with place and community
sacred_places: Mount Fuji and other sacred landscapes

records.name: Zoroastrian traditions
records.origin: Ancient Iranian religious tradition associated with Zarathustra/Zoroaster
records.core: Ahura Mazda, truth/order, ethical choice and cosmic struggle in Zoroastrian traditions

records.name: African traditional religions
records.origin: Many distinct local and regional traditions with deep historical roots; no single founder
records.core: diverse relationships among creator beings, spirits, ancestors, community, land and ritual
sacred_places: locally defined sacred groves, rivers, shrines and landscapes
countries: many African countries and diaspora communities

records.name: Indigenous religious traditions
records.origin: Many distinct place-based traditions; no single founder or universal theology
records.core: land, ancestors, community, spirits, ritual, ecological relationships and inherited knowledge in diverse forms
countries: many countries across the Americas, Arctic, Oceania, Africa and Asia

records.name: Folk and popular religious traditions
records.origin: Local traditions combining inherited ritual, sacred places, ancestors, saints, spirits and community practice
records.core: highly variable; often place-based and mixed with major religious traditions
schools: regional traditions rather than one denomination
sacred_places: local shrines, springs, mountains, groves, tombs and pilgrimage sites
countries: global; especially useful as a country-level residual layer where survey/census categories permit

records.name: New religious movements
records.origin: Primarily modern-period movements with diverse origins
records.core: highly variable; often new revelation, reinterpretation, syncretism, charismatic leadership or alternative practice

records.name: Atheism
records.origin: Multiple philosophical and cultural histories; not a single organization or religion
records.core: lack of belief in gods, with positions ranging from positive denial to non-belief without metaphysical commitment

records.name: Agnosticism
records.origin: Modern philosophical category associated with questions about knowledge of the divine
records.core: limits or uncertainty concerning knowledge of gods or ultimate reality

records.name: Secular humanism
records.origin: Modern humanist and secular intellectual traditions
records.core: human dignity, reason, ethics, flourishing and civic responsibility without requiring supernatural belief

next_depth: For each record, instantiate the full blueprint: source corpus, doctrinal matrix, ritual/practice layer, institutions, sacred places, country composition, demographic observations, legal status, historical events, relationships, and time-series evidence.
